subject: HW fit: Cobalt Labs Dedicated Capacity — memory vs throughput tradeoffs
messages:
From: Ethan Ross <ethan@cobaltlabs.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alyssa Chang <procurement@cobaltlabs.ai>
Date: Thu, 01 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Sizing guidance request — CobaltSumm (long context)

Hi Soojin / Ben,

Thanks for taking this on. Quick intro: Cobalt Labs is building CobaltSumm, an automated clinical summarization and Q&A product. Key constraints:
- Model: internal fine-tuned ~70B decoder model (fp16), often run with ~50k token context windows for multi-document summaries.
- Latency SLO: 300ms p50 / aim for <800ms p99 for single-request interactive flows.
- Peak QPS expectation: 35 qps synchronous, average 8 qps; bursts up to 120 qps for scheduled batch jobs.
- Cost sensitivity: we want to understand reserve vs. burst economics; likely looking at a 12–24 month reserved commitment.
- Compliance: must run in a dedicated environment (isolation, audit logs).

Can you recommend a hardware mix and an initial committed configuration (H100 vs A100 vs L4), and an ops plan for fallbacks? I attached a short deck with traffic shapes.

Would appreciate a short call next week to align on profiling and mutual action plan.

Best,
Ethan
CTO, Cobalt Labs
Attachment: Cobalt_Deck_Q2.pdf

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Ethan Ross <ethan@cobaltlabs.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 02 Apr 2027 11:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sizing guidance request — CobaltSumm (long context)

Thanks Ethan — good detail, this is exactly the right starting point. High level guidance up front:

- H100 (80GB) -> preferred when you need large KV cache + >40k token context with minimal model quantization. Best p99 tail and predictable latency for single-threaded long-context inference. Higher unit cost but fewer GPUs for very large models.
- A100 (80GB) -> strong middle-ground for medium-long contexts (8k–32k) and higher throughput with batching. If you can quantize to 8-bit and shard, you get good cost/throughput.
- L4 (48GB equivalent in our offering) -> cost-efficient for smaller models, parallel replicas, and offloading embedding/serving/replicas for burst workloads. Lower memory headroom; not ideal for 50k token KV cache.

Given your traffic (interactive low-latency + large batch peaks) I recommend a hybrid: reserve H100 capacity sized for steady-state long-context interactive sessions (handles the memory headroom), reserve A100 for throughput and mid-context workloads, and a pool of L4s for inexpensive scaled replicas / batch work.

I've attached a quick SKU matrix (sku-matrix-v1.xlsx) with rough capacity mapping and unit-costs. Next steps:
1) Dev-led profiling (we can run a 48–72 hour profiling run with a sampled model/weights in our dedicated staging to capture KV cache and per-token throughput) — Dev, can you pick two representative checkpoints?
2) Ops: target initial committed mix + burst policy. Ben, happy if you take the procurement lead here.
3) Schedule a 30m call — propose Tue Apr 6 10:00 PT.

On the call we can walk tradeoffs and show latency-cost curves for H100 vs A100 vs L4 at several context sizes.

— Soojin
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachment: sku-matrix-v1.xlsx

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ethan Ross <ethan@cobaltlabs.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 03 Apr 2027 08:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sizing guidance request — CobaltSumm (long context)

Adding some numbers to ground the discussion (rough, based on our recent benchmarks):

- Example config assumptions: 70B fp16 (no quant) -> ~60–70GB GPU memory to hold model + KV workingset; with 50k context and 1k request window you need ~2–3x additional headroom for KV cache and batching. H100-80GB gives the simplest path without model surgery.
- Throughput samples (single request, streaming generation): H100-80GB: ~18–25 tokens/sec single-thread long-context (depends on decode strategy). A100-80GB with quantized weights (8-bit) can reach ~30–40 tokens/sec in batched scenarios for 30k contexts. L4 (quantized 8-bit, smaller models ~13–30B) can do ~80–120 tokens/sec for lightweight Q&A/embeddings.
- Cost ballpark (cloud equivalent unit): H100: $X.XX/hr reserved pricing baseline, A100: ~$0.65–0.85 * H100 price (depends on region), L4: ~0.12–0.18 * H100 (cheaper). We will provide precise numbers in the cost-estimates.csv attachment.
- Ops notes: prefix/KV caching is your biggest win on cost if many requests share context. We recommend: persistent prefix cache + routing policy that routes long-context requests to H100 and shorter/quantizable requests to A100/L4. Also plan for an autoscaling burst pool of L4s to absorb batch jobs.

What I need from Cobalt:
- Two model checkpoints (full and quantized if available) for profiling.
- Representative trace of typical sessions (token lengths distribution).

If you’re open, Redwood can run the profiling in a dedicated staging cluster (IAM-restricted) and return measured latency curves, resource utilization, and suggested reserve counts.

— Dev
Senior Inference Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachment: cost-estimates.csv

Appreciate the rapid and detailed responses. Two quick asks before the call:
1) Can you produce a simple visualization (tradeoff matrix) that shows cost vs p99 latency for H100 vs A100 vs L4 across three context sizes: 8k, 32k, 50k? That helps our execs.
2) Looping in Alyssa from procurement — we may be able to commit to a 12-month reserved block if the numbers line up.

We’ll prepare model checkpoints this week. Tue Apr 6 at 10:00 PT works for us.

Ethan

Subject: Re: Sizing guidance request — CobaltSumm (long context)

Ethan / Alyssa — thanks for the quick turnaround. I pulled the attached weighted SKU selection matrix together and a recommended initial committed mix for a 12-month reserve based on the inputs so far. Summary (initial proposal):

- Initial reserved baseline (12m): 6 x H100-80GB, 8 x A100-80GB, 20 x L4 (reserve can be tiered into steady/burst pools).
  - Rationale: H100 baseline covers steady-state long-context interactive users with KV caching headroom. A100 supports bulk throughput and batched mid-context workloads. L4s are low-cost for embeddings, async batch processing, and overflow.
- Burst policy: additional L4 spot/ephemeral pool + autoscale A100 capacity for mid-context bursts.
- Estimated committed monthly spend range: see cost-estimates.csv (we included both reserved & burst blended scenarios).
- Ops commitments: 2-week profiling window, 1 production pilot (1 month), then scale to reserve.

Next steps:
1) Confirm profiling dates and provide model artifacts.
2) Procurement: Alyssa, if you share target budget range, Ben can draft commitment options and term sheets.
3) I will book Tue Apr 6 10:00 PT for the technical + procurement alignment.

If that sounds OK I will circulate a one-page mutual action plan post-call.

— Neha Kapoor
Director, Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
